topIssues.title: fix(lifeops): accept explicit empty subjects for knowledge-only household grants
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Reproduced failure

The deployed Bettina pilot at `40bf83d22b150d71632878b3868097cc51ccd713` now discovers and invokes the requested household action. A real owner request for `HOUSEHOLD_COORDINATION_ISSUE_GRANT` supplied `subjectEntityIds: []` with `scopes: ["knowledge.read"]`, a persisted synthetic caregiver role and an explicit household/principal. The action returned `MISSING_HOUSEHOLD_PARAMETERS` naming `subjectEntityIds` even though that parameter was supplied. A subsequent owner export independently confirmed that no household grant was stored for the synthetic principal.

The generic `resolveActionArgs` presence check treats every empty required array as missing. `HouseholdCoordinationService.issueGrant` deliberately permits an empty subject list for a knowledge-only grant; it separately rejects non-owner calendar grants without subjects. The action resolver prevents this valid domain contract from reaching the service.

## Acceptance

- Preserve the distinction between an omitted parameter and an explicitly supplied empty array for action parameters whose domain allows empty lists.
- Allow the household knowledge-only grant with explicit `subjectEntityIds: []` through the real owner action path and persist the actual grant.
- Keep omitted subjects, malformed arrays, unauthorized principals/roles, out-of-relationship subjects and non-owner calendar grants without subjects rejected by their existing boundaries. Do not make all required arrays optional or silently default an omitted array to empty.
- Cover the resolver and promoted household action with meaningful regression tests, run owning package/root and hosted checks, and complete the paired-guest read/revoke/expiry/export acceptance on the deployed pilot.

Part of #30123, #31172 and #31162. The action-discovery repair #31181 is separately verified: it successfully executes the role binding and exposes this downstream parameter defect.

topIssues.title: fix(app-core): authenticate owner browser WebSockets with the session cookie
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Reproduced failure

On the Bettina HTTPS pilot at `58cd2df949d37627131de2427ca043e218385e09`, a normal owner password login succeeds and authenticated `GET /api/status` returns 200 with `canRespond: true`. A same-origin browser WebSocket using that session closes with code 1008, `Unauthorized`, after a ping instead of receiving a pong. The backend recorded 36 pre-auth message rejections during a fresh 50-second observation.

The app-core WebSocket authorizer checks query/header session tokens but omits the first-party browser session cookie. REST and WebSocket authentication consequently disagree for a normal browser login.

## Acceptance

- Admit a current owner browser session through the canonical session store and role resolution, retaining the existing origin boundary.
- Reject expired, revoked, malformed, unknown and non-owner cookie sessions; do not introduce a trusted-loopback or missing-origin shortcut for cookie admission.
- Preserve existing bearer/device authentication behavior and fail closed on store errors.
- Exercise the real HTTP/WebSocket boundary and session storage, run package/root checks and exact-head hosted checks, and repeat password-login plus same-origin ping/pong on the deployed pilot. Keep credentials out of evidence.

Part of Bettina deployment acceptance in #30123. This is separate from the model action-discovery repair #31181 and from the cloud/native session-authority work in #30920, which does not change this host authorizer.

topIssues.title: feat(lifeops): export agreement originals with provenance and audit history
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Observed gap

Bettina's PDD KNOW-8 requires the owner to export the original agreement, reviewed obligations, hashes, pins, grants and audit history. The verification plan requires an independently re-hashed manifest export. Current `AgreementKnowledgeService.readOwnerPdf` and `GET /api/lifeops/agreements/:id/download` return only the verified PDF bytes. `FamilyOperationsView` has review, pin and guest controls but no export journey. There is no agreement export manifest or agreement mutation audit trail in the current service.

## Acceptance

- Provide an owner-authenticated export for one immutable agreement version containing the exact original PDF and a versioned manifest of source metadata/page map, all obligation review states and citations, pins, grants and available audit history. Do not expose credentials or infer guest permission from a pin.
- Verify original byte length and SHA-256 before export; unavailable or mismatched bytes fail visibly. Provide a manifest integrity contract that an independent reader can verify.
- Reuse the canonical audit ledger for agreement upload/extraction, review, pin/unpin, grant/revoke and export events. Preserve actor, artifact version/content identity and state transitions. Do not fabricate missing legacy history; represent its coverage explicitly.
- Keep the manifest internally consistent during concurrent review, pin and grant changes. Do not add another file store, scheduler or shadow audit system.
- Expose the download through the real Family Operations UI with visible loading/error states and an original-download option. Exercise denied-principal and corrupt/missing-storage paths.
- Real PGlite regression, owning package gates, root verification and exact-head hosted checks pass. On the pilot, export a synthetic agreement after review/pin/grant activity, independently hash and inspect its contents, and attach sanitized UI/network/video evidence.

This implements the missing KNOW-8 journey under #30123. Broader workspace export (AUDIT-4), dependency-aware deletion (AUDIT-5/AUDIT-7), verified guest live acceptance and final merged MVP deployment remain separate acceptance requirements; this issue does not stand in for them. Selected-correspondence intake remains owned by #31063/#31032.

topIssues.title: feat(lifeops): export and delete a reviewed family workspace
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Observed missing product flow

The Bettina PDD requires a workspace export (AUDIT-4), a dependency preview before deletion (AUDIT-5), immediate revocation (AUDIT-6), and documented primary/derived/cache/backup purge behavior (AUDIT-7). The merged agreement export in #31165 covers one source artifact and its review/access history. `AgreementKnowledgeService` and the owner Family Operations routes have no workspace lifecycle/dependency-preview/delete flow. The owner therefore cannot complete the PDD's export-and-delete test workspace journey from the product.

## Acceptance

- Provide an owner-only manifest export joining the selected family workspace's immutable source artifacts, hashes, reviewed obligations, packet versions/approvals, and recorded calendar/message receipts. Preserve provenance and distinguish unavailable legacy history; never include credentials or fabricate receipts.
- Before deletion, show the exact affected source versions, pins, obligations, authority baselines, workflows, packets, and local calendar dependencies. Bind confirmation to the reviewed dependency snapshot; reject stale previews and concurrent additions instead of silently broadening deletion.
- Document and implement the revocation/deletion ordering and retention policy across primary bytes, derived records, cached projections, and eligible backups. Retained audit/receipt metadata must be explicit and must not retain deleted private source content. Provider events/messages and unrelated workspaces must not be deleted implicitly.
- Expose the journey through the real owner UI with loading, denied, stale-preview, partial-failure, and completion states. Guest grants, pinned context, links, and downloads must lose access at the documented revocation boundary.
- Prove the behavior with real storage/integration tests, owning package and root gates, exact-head hosted checks, and a synthetic live pilot workspace with independently inspected export and post-deletion reads. Preserve unrelated live family data and the original messaging service.

Part of #30123. Complements #31162 and #31172; it does not replace the remaining live Google, school-workflow, messaging, or final merged-deployment acceptance. Selected-correspondence intake remains in #31063/#31032.

topIssues.title: fix(lifeops): make household actions available to authenticated owner planning
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
On the deployed Bettina pilot, a password-authenticated owner cannot reliably invoke household role binding/grant actions from a new conversation, although the runtime inventory contains the umbrella and promoted direct actions.

Observed on combined revision `58cd2df949d37627131de2427ca043e218385e09`:
- `/api/runtime` reports 477 registered actions, including `HOUSEHOLD_COORDINATION`, `HOUSEHOLD_COORDINATION_BIND_ROLE`, and `HOUSEHOLD_COORDINATION_ISSUE_GRANT`.
- An owner request to bind a clearly labeled synthetic caregiver and issue only `knowledge.read` instead selected a calendar view interaction and reminder actions; it did not create a household grant. The synthetic once reminders were subsequently absent from inventory; deletion/readback returned 404.
- A fresh owner conversation explicitly requested only the registered direct bind-role action, prohibited substitute effects, and permitted action discovery. It returned no actions and said the action was unavailable.

The root cause is not established. Inspect authenticated owner attribution, disclosure gates, action validation/discovery, and the actual model input before changing policy. Do not bypass owner authorization or add a generic action-execution escape hatch.

Acceptance:
- A normal authenticated owner conversation can bind a synthetic household role and issue/revoke a scoped household grant using the existing domain actions, with persisted receipts and no substitute reminders or external sends.
- Wrong/guest/unverified principals remain denied; action discovery and owner-private data do not leak across audiences.
- Record the real model input/output and persisted action/audit results, then complete owning-package, root, and exact-head hosted checks for the actual fix.

Related: #30123, #31172, #31162. This blocks the live grant lifecycle acceptance; no real guest was contacted.

topPRs.title: release: promote staging Dedicated onboarding and login fixes to production
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Promote the certified staging app and Cloud stack to production so Google sign-in hands the user back to the correct account and agent selection, an intentional shutdown stays stopped, explicit Start restores the latest saved conversation, and a slow OAuth callback can finish before its socket closes.

This is the accumulated staging release: main `5525597f50e7792fe105b79cff06ecb69c364317` to staging `e7132455cef8aa1ff8e9dc086d8528eb39b34721`, spanning 1,402 commits and 4,226 files. The clean merge preview is exactly certified tree `8c979bb5837bde91a3ff263946ad9523068c63b8`.

Validation:

- [Canonical staging release 34682808715](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/34682808715) passed API deployment, consolidated Pages deployment, routing, and the real deployed Dedicated identity/chat/history trajectory. Its certificate was issued September 12 at 08:42:36 UTC and expires September 26. Repository, source, workflow hash, expiry, and the production merge tree were checked against the artifact.
- The deployed renderer produced a settled real assistant reply in 30,358 ms. Reload and fresh-browser history passed with the same Personal identity, runtime binding, and API base; no forbidden agent mutations occurred. This is not a response-latency completion claim.
- Actual authorized Google sign-in and fresh entry passed. All 26 conversation entries matched after desktop and mobile reloads in both the hosted app and ordinary local bun run dev. Earlier normal shutdown/explicit Start preserved a fresh backup and subsequent history. A few pre-fix test turns lost before the backup repair remain unrecovered.
- Login PR #31108 passed all hosted checks. Its real delayed callback regression failed before the socket-timeout fix and passed afterward; the original redirect succeeds and a replay is rejected. The login build and 614 package tests passed, with one PostgreSQL-only test explicitly skipped, plus typecheck, lint, and full root verification.
- A production backup was fully restored and the canonical eleven pending migrations rehearsed: ledger 358 to 369, preserving 176 users and 100 agents. The clone used PostgreSQL18.6/pgvector0.8.6 versus live18.4/0.8.2; roles/ACL restoration was not tested. The preserved backup and rehearsal receipts remain available.

Broader PR CI is not all green. Observed failures include two Home fixtures missing the real client's onAuthorityChange method, a wallet-spacing visibility assertion, OCR classification, deterministic tool scenarios, and the mock walkthrough's mobile wallet-capability toggle. These remain failures; the Dedicated browser evidence above does not certify those separate features.

Deployment sequencing:

- Use the protected production Cloud workflow and exact-tree certification; its canonical migration step precedes the API deployment.
- Deploy the provisioning worker separately from the same promoted main source and pin the tested immutable EF59 agent image. Production R2 storage passed a private 2 MiB round trip. Prepared configuration holds automatic fleet upgrades and orphan deletion; the canonical worker workflow defaults the currently absent warm-pool flag to disabled.
- Activate one explicitly provisioned, hardware-attested Dedicated slot. Existing agents and their data are preserved. The prepared ccx13 request is EUR43.49/month including IPv4, with one slot and a firewall restricted to the production control plane; no paid node exists yet.
- Complete the production hosting-confirmation, provisioning, real-reply, reload and lifecycle UI run. Google entry was verified against the old production app and exposed its automatic-opening/insufficient-credit error. The selected founder account now has one recorded USD2 internal test-credit grant, verified in the billing UI; no card was charged.

First-ever Google signup still needs an unused authorized identity. Shared/Telegram and native-device releases remain outside this Dedicated acceptance run.

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): finish Dedicated sign-in and lifecycle recovery
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Dedicated onboarding and lifecycle management could lose Cloud account status, cancel accepted shutdowns, immediately restart an intentionally stopped agent, or leave local Google sign-in stuck on Connecting. This change restores the account display through the trusted control plane, preserves accepted shutdown ownership across worker bookkeeping, and requires an explicit Start after a user-requested stop. Settings keeps queued lifecycle progress visible until the requested state is observed and recognizes a managed Dedicated selection as active.

Direct localhost staging login now uses the existing hosted CLI handoff so Google receives its approved callback. The app preserves safe return destinations, clears account-scoped bindings during explicit switching, and claims the one-time login result only after React Strict Mode startup settles. The regression failed before the fix with no stored session and passes afterward with exactly one claim and cleared busy state.

Validation: 98 account tests, 38 heartbeat/recovery tests, 83 lifecycle dispatch/recovery tests, 83 proxy/pairing/intent tests, 24 recovery tests, and 34 management tests passed during development. The latest authentication and account-routing group passes 133 tests. Its regression failed before the fix: a returned staging session was overwritten by the local runtime's disconnected status. It now verifies the staging account while preserving the local runtime URL and credential; unrelated remote and unstamped local clients retain their existing route. Full repository verification passed on the previous head 3c58019301464ed0009199c83b8ebb048354fb81; the final full run on f5901ab5092f2b4ac3fb7176b0fb14bd312b7915, tree 2be56f3c65317db8d2745ba79a6f180420176a3c passed with exit 0. Current-head hosted checks are pending; the repository owner authorized the accelerated maintainer merge path using this exact local verification and the relevant regression tests. Pending hosted CI is not claimed as passing. The canonical full staging deployment and renderer proof remain required.

Live staging evidence: the requested Gmail account completed Google sign-in, actual Dedicated model replies, and conversation continuity after reload at desktop/mobile widths in the local and hosted apps. A real shutdown saved a 9,948,577-byte private R2 backup and removed the container; the backup passed decryption and manifest verification, and history plus a new model reply survived recreation. Final stay-stopped and explicit Start acceptance awaits deployment. Fresh-account signup and production rollout are not claimed. The broad visual audit was stopped after an unrelated Tasks/iPad timeout; no all-views pass is claimed.


Latest local browser acceptance: after the CLI login return, the requested account remains connected on Settings reload, its Dedicated agent is active, all prior conversation exchanges are present, and a new real reply correctly recalled the project and kickoff day. Inspected the mobile rendering. The failed pre-fix browser request was /api/cloud/status (404); after the fix the authenticated /api/v1/user request succeeds.

topPRs.title: feat(plugin-local-inference): wire the Apple Foundation Models fast path on iOS (#31118)
topPRs.author: hermesagent270-commits
topPRs.body:
## Summary

`registerAppleFoundationAdapter` / `getAppleFoundationAdapter` in `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/backends/apple-foundation.ts` had no production writer or reader, so the iOS 26 Apple Foundation Models fast path the module header, `docs/per-platform-backend-strategy.md` and the adapter test all describe never activated. This wires it, keeping llama.cpp as the owned backend.

New `src/runtime/apple-foundation-fast-path.ts`:

- `tryRegisterAppleFoundationAdapter({ platform, getBridge })` runs at mobile boot (`registerLocalInferenceBoot`, before the local handler installs). It registers the adapter only when `ELIZA_PLATFORM=ios`, the bridge handle exists, and `bridge.probe()` reports `capabilities.foundationModel === true`; every other outcome is returned as a typed skip reason and logged at debug.
- `resolveIosComputerUseBridge()` reads `Capacitor.Plugins.ComputerUse` locally (mirroring computeruse's `getIosBridge`). A runtime import of `@elizaos/plugin-computeruse/mobile/ios-bridge` is not possible: that package publishes `dist/mobile/` as declarations only, and the plugin's vitest alias maps the package root to `src/index.ts`. The type import stays.
- `resolveAppleFoundationFastPath(modelType, params)` is consulted at the top of the local text handler (`makeHandler` now receives the model type). It returns the adapter only for `ModelType.TEXT_SMALL` and `TEXT_COMPLETION` with a non-empty prompt of at most 4000 characters, no streaming (`stream`, `streamStructured`, `onStreamChunk`), no structured decoding (`grammar`, `responseSkeleton`, `spanSamplerPlan`, `prefill`), and no non-text `responseFormat`. `ACTION_PLANNER` and `RESPONSE_HANDLER` share the TEXT_SMALL slot but never take it. `ELIZA_APPLE_FOUNDATION_FAST_PATH=0|false|off` disables the route.
- `generateWithAppleFoundation` maps `prompt`, `maxTokens` and `temperature` onto `foundationModelGenerate`, returns the text, and throws on a bridge failure (no empty-string success).

The adapter test's "runtime side wires this up" comment and the backend-strategy doc now describe the real wiring.

Closes #31118

## Evidence

- `apple-foundation-fast-path.test.ts` (new, 9 cases): bridge resolution from a fake `Capacitor` global; registration on iOS with `foundationModel:true`; skips for non-iOS, missing bridge, `probe.ok:false`, a throwing probe, and `foundationModel:false` (registry stays null); eligibility matrix for model types, prompt length, streaming and structured-decoding params; env kill switch; not-yet-available adapter declined; generate mapping and failure propagation.
- `ensure-local-inference-handler.test.ts` (new case): with an adapter registered, the registered TEXT_SMALL handler returns the adapter's text and never calls the engine; the ACTION_PLANNER handler and a streaming TEXT_SMALL call still reach `localInferenceEngine.generate`.
- `boot.test.ts` (2 new cases): on a mobile platform with `ELIZA_PLATFORM=ios` the registration runs with `platform: "ios"` before the handler install; on desktop it is never attempted.
- `bunx vitest run` on the four touched suites: 53/53. `bun run test` in `plugins/plugin-local-inference`: 3005 passed, 2 skipped (285 files). `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint:check`: clean.
- Root `bun run verify`: running on this branch; result will be posted as a comment.

**Not exercised: a real iOS 26 device.** The bridge contract (`probe`, `foundationModelGenerate`) is the existing `IosComputerUseBridge` interface implemented in `ComputerUseBridge.swift`; the tests drive it through a fake. On a device, the boot log states whether the fast path registered and, per call, `[local-inference] apple-foundation served N->M tokens in Xms`.
